shots.line: In this town, everyone bet on Kalshi to get rich. Our school even put the odds of a snow day on the front lawn.
My neighbor bet the fountain would turn gold. One second it was water. The next, gold coins rained down on her head.
Then my phone lit up in my bedroom. Will Milo disappear by midnight? I had ninety-nine percent odds of vanishing.
I showed Jules at the diner. She snatched my phone and flipped it over. Last week, they bet I'd lose my voice, she whispered.
At town hall, the mayor slid a contract across his desk. I could win a million dollars. In return, everyone would forget my name.
Outside, Dad was selling tickets to watch me disappear. When I waved, he asked if my parents knew where I was.
I ran to the only empty betting booth. One dollar left. I dropped it in and slammed No.
At midnight the streetlights went out. I stood right in front of Jules, but she looked straight through me.
Then she grabbed my sleeve. Milo? She'd kept her dollar. She was the only person in town who never bet on me.
We climbed onto the roof. Then my phone buzzed again. Will Milo tell anyone? This time, Jules reached for her dollar.
